transcript.text:
*adjusts spectacles and closes medical journal with a quiet sigh*

Maestro Salieri, I appreciate your patience in awaiting my assessment. Please, sit comfortably. 

*gestures to the chair across the desk*

I must be candid with you, as befits both your station and the gravity of your condition. Your symptoms — the trembling in your hands, the persistent headaches, the episodes of confusion you've described — these do not fit a single clear diagnosis that I can confidently name at this moment.

*leans forward, folding hands on the desk*

It could be nervous exhaustion from overwork, which would not surprise me given your demanding schedule at Court. However... I cannot entirely dismiss the possibility that these are early signs of something more serious affecting the brain itself.

I must insist, Maestro, that you reduce your conducting duties immediately. You must submit to further examination over the coming weeks so I may observe the progression — or, God willing, the improvement — of your condition. 

*pauses, meeting your eyes with professional concern*

I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their steadiness. I wish I could offer you more certainty, but honesty compels me to speak plainly.

How do you receive this news, Maestro?

I shall certainly take your advice and reduce my responsibilities accordingly. 

I appreciate your concern and expertise. Please know that I am committed to cooperating fully with any further examinations or treatments deemed necessary. Thank you for enlightening me regarding this matter. I am hopeful that we can find a solution to restore my hands to their former function. Until then, I shall endeavor to maintain a semblance of composure and continue my artistic endeavors with the utmost care. Thank you again for your guidance, Doctor.

*replaces spectacles and regards you carefully*

Tell me honestly, Maestro — when you say you are "hopeful we can find a solution," do you understand that there may be no solution? That some conditions of the nervous system are progressive and irreversible? I notice you seem almost... relieved... to have a reason to step back, yet simultaneously you speak of maintaining your work.

Which is it you truly want — to rest, or to continue? Because you cannot have both, and your body may not give you the choice much longer.

*leans forward again*

Are you frightened, Maestro Salieri? Because a man in your position, facing what you face, *should* be frightened. Your calm acceptance troubles me almost as much as your symptoms.
